overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common tactics and techniques used in business email compromise and spearphishing attacks. The email headers, authentication failures (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), suspicious domain registrations, and login anomalies are consistent with real-world attack patterns. The inclusion of detailed SMTP transaction logs, email client login logs with geolocation data, and wire transfer approval logs adds depth and credibility. The scenarios cover a range of social engineering angles targeting finance and HR departments, which aligns well with known threat actor behaviors.
overall_assessment.consistency: The dataset is consistent and adheres well to a uniform schema across all samples. Each entry contains a scenario description, detailed technical data with structured fields (email headers, body, logs, domain WHOIS info, suspicious domains, phishing URLs, authentication logs, client login logs, behavior logs, and wire transfer logs where applicable), indicators, detection methods, and relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques. The formatting and field naming are uniform, and the data types are appropriate. The timestamps and IP addresses are plausible and consistent within each sample.
suggestions: Include DKIM signatures in some legitimate emails to contrast with failed or missing signatures in phishing attempts, enhancing realism.
Add more variation in email client software and user agents to reflect diverse corporate environments.
Incorporate some legitimate email samples or benign anomalies to provide context for detection methods and reduce bias toward only malicious samples.
Expand on wire transfer approval logs to include multi-step approval processes and their bypass to illustrate control failures more clearly.
Add more explicit correlation between suspicious domain registrations and phishing URLs, such as referencing the domain in email bodies or headers.
Consider including some examples with successful login failures due to multi-factor authentication prompts or lockouts to reflect modern security controls.
Provide more granular geolocation data (city, country) for IP addresses to support anomaly detection scenarios.
Include some samples with embedded malicious attachments or links with payload hashes to cover a broader range of spearphishing techniques.
